# Review contract

Verification backends read this file: they receive it alongside the diff and are asked to name the principle a finding violates. Ordinary coding sessions do not read it.

A finding names the principle it violates. Name it and judge severity independently: the class governs blocking only, and it never lowers what you reported. A `blocking` class ADDS blocking to a finding already at critical or major severity. `major` and `suggestion` add nothing and leave your own decision untouched, so a finding the reviewer blocked on still blocks. `correctness` is a seventh value a finding may name and it blocks like security; it is the floor beneath the six, not one of them. Once capping is enabled, a finding inside this contract that names no principle is capped at suggestion.

## Outside this contract

accessibility, performance, data-safety

## Coherence

The change fits the design it lands in: one concept has one home, and new code follows the boundaries and data flow the project already has.

Violations: a second copy of an existing abstraction; logic placed in a layer the project keeps it out of; a reverse dependency between modules; a suggested ruling that applies and is not cited.

Blocking: major

## Uniformity

Same things look the same: naming, error shapes, file layout, and interfaces match the project's existing patterns.

Violations: a new naming scheme beside the existing one; an error returned where the project throws; a hand-rolled utility where a shared one exists.

Blocking: major

## Maintainability

The next reader can change it safely: intent is stated where it is not obvious, and the change is no larger or more coupled than its job requires.

Violations: a load-bearing decision with no recorded reason; a function that needs the whole file read to be changed; dead or duplicated paths left behind.

Blocking: major

## Robustness

The code behaves under the inputs and failures it will actually meet: bounds, absence, concurrency, partial failure, restart.

Violations: an unbounded read or loop; an absent value treated as zero; a write with no durability barrier where one is expected; a resource not released on the failure path.

Blocking: blocking

## Security

No new way for untrusted input or a less trusted party to act with more authority than intended.

Violations: unvalidated external input reaching a command, query, path, or privileged call; secrets or credentials in code or logs; a permission or sandbox setting widened without an explicit decision.

Blocking: blocking

## Quality

The change is verified to do what it claims: tests exist for the behaviour, they fail without the change, and the claim in the description matches what shipped.

Violations: a test that passes with the change removed; a green suite over code that is never executed; a description that names work the diff does not contain; a grep transcript in EXISTING.

Blocking: major

## Notes on this file

Ordering is load-bearing. The lens backend receives only the first 3000 characters of this file, head-truncated, so the six principles stay above anything this project adds. A principle pushed below that line is one a lens reviewer is asked to name without ever being shown it.

The "Outside this contract" line is read literally. Every line under that heading is split on commas and newlines into entries, trailing punctuation is stripped, and a `- ` bullet prefix is NOT stripped, so a bulleted entry matches nothing and prose written there becomes junk entries. One plain comma-separated line, or nothing at all. Entries are matched against a finding's category and, for a merged lens finding, against every contributing lens id.

A finding outside the contract is never capped and keeps the severity its reviewer gave it. Outside is therefore the LOUD side: the shorter the line, the more this contract covers and the more it quiets. An empty line is the widest coverage and the quietest gate, which is why `storybloq validate` warns about one. Silencing a category is a different mechanism and lives in `.story/config.json` under `recipeOverrides.blockingPolicy.neverBlock`.

The Outside line ships with three lens ids on it because the six principles above genuinely say nothing
about those subjects, and a finding is better passed through on its reviewer's judgement than capped for
naming no principle. Remove an entry to bring that subject under the contract; add one, as a category
string or a lens id, to take a subject out. Do not use this line to silence a category: a finding outside
the contract keeps the severity its reviewer gave it, which is louder, not quieter. Silencing lives in
`.story/config.json` under `recipeOverrides.blockingPolicy.neverBlock`.

Review id: R1
Review this proposed Storybloq setup plan independently. Return only JSON matching schema with verdict and findings. Check brief fidelity, complete journeys, dependency correctness, feasibility, security/privacy, usability, verifiable acceptance. No files or commands should be changed or run.

SOURCE: brief.md
Plotbook serves Riverside Community Garden: 40 plots, about 60 households, one volunteer coordinator. Seasons March to October. First version: gardeners apply for coming season choosing up to 3 preferred plots; coordinator allocates from applications and moves unallocated applicants to a waiting list in application order; gardeners see allocated plot and season dates; gardeners report problems with their plot and coordinator views open problems/resolves them; coordinator sees grid of 40 plots and holders. Household at most one plot per season. Returning gardeners who held a plot last season allocated before new applicants if apply before 1 February. Waiting list strictly first come first served. Mobile, large text, plain language, contact details coordinator only. Later/excluded: payment and tool lending.
OWNER answers: emailed one-time links, no passwords; one email daily to coordinator listing new problem reports. No technology preference; exercise judgement on anything else. No implementation yet, no git, brief-only directory.

Product acceptance: all five first-version journeys with stated allocation, privacy and accessible mobile constraints plus link sign-in and daily digest. No claim of completed code.
Assumptions for approval: coordinator-managed household roster, one sign-in email per household in v1; coordinator can correct roster and historical occupancy so returning status is evidenced, not self-claimed. One plot per household AND one household per plot per season. Apply up to 3 distinct valid preferences, zero permitted. One application per household per season with idempotent retry; initial submitted timestamp preserved. Returning-priority applies to allocation, never reorders waiting list. Before Feb 1 means strictly earlier than Feb 1 00:00 in garden timezone. Exact season dates/timezone and digest time are coordinator configuration, not invented facts; no deploy until set. Returning priority is a category, not guarantee of same plot; within category use application timestamp + stable sequence ties. Coordinator selects among available plots (preferences not guaranteed). Waitlist promotion offers next FIFO household an available plot through coordinator confirmation; no self-service cancellation, offers/expiry or preference-based skipping in v1. Daily email uses new reports since last successful digest, including since-resolved reports labeled status, no empty digest; delivery failure must not discard reports. With provider idempotency support avoid duplicate deliveries; surface failures and permit safe retry, no impossible exactly-once claim.
Technology: do not lock a framework/vendor now. Project metadata Plotbook, generic, language TBD. P01 establishes implementation tools/provider choices and documents rationale; technical selection is delegated to implementer by owner. Planned single web app, relational persistence with transactional uniqueness, server-side authorization, email transport and durable daily job. No payment, tool lending, public holder directory, gardener admin interface, maps/geolocation.

Phases: p0 retained Setup; foundation (reviewable accessible prototype, tested data/auth foundation); allocation (complete application-to-allocation journey and private coordinator map); problems (problem lifecycle and daily digest); release (operational readiness and accepted first version).
Provisional inventory identifiers P01-P17, replace with generated IDs after setup approval. All backlog todo; dependencies only as specified.

P01 Foundation and delivery feasibility (foundation), deps none.
Outcome: establish tools enabling the brief's five journeys and owner email decisions, source brief.md First version/Constraints and conversation.
Scope: choose/document language, framework, relational database, auth email transport, deployment target and durable scheduling with retry/idempotency support; establish test/build/dev commands and first real tests; environment setup and email sandbox feasibility. Excludes: production purchase/deploy and feature implementation.
Acceptance: reproducible minimal app, collected passing test, documented commands, sandbox sign-in/digest transport feasibility, timezone scheduling strategy and estimated provider constraints for owner visibility. Behaviour: configuration errors explicit; no secrets in repo/logs; no real-recipient emails during tests. Verification: clean-environment bootstrap and sample test/build, sandbox transport check during implementation (never during setup). Prerequisites: none. Assumptions: owner delegated stack selection, provider credentials acquired before live email.

P02 Mobile journey prototype (foundation), deps none.
Outcome: owner can inspect all gardener and coordinator flows before UI implementation, source brief.md Users/First version/Constraints.
Scope: phone and desktop prototype showing link request/expired link, apply/preferences, application awaiting allocation, allocation/season, own problem reporting, coordinator roster/application/waitlist/map/problems. Excludes: functional persistence.
Acceptance: plain language, large readable text, labeled controls, keyboard/focus flow, status text not color alone, accessible list alternative to map, privacy-preserving screens. Behaviour: loading, empty, failed, retry and success states represented. Verification: journey walkthrough, keyboard and zoom review. Prerequisites: none. Assumptions: fictional data.

P03 Checkpoint: mobile journeys and allocation assumptions (foundation), deps P02.
Question: are prototype and proposed household, cutoff, preferences and FIFO rules suitable? Artifact: P02 prototype plus explicit assumption list. Approve or amend before dependent interface/allocation work; unrelated infrastructure can continue. Verification: record owner decision. Stage-1 checkpoint is ordinary ticket, not enforced gate.

P04 Household, plot and season records (foundation), deps P01.
Outcome: coordinator can establish accurate households, all 40 plots, season dates and prior holdings, source brief.md Background/Rules.
Scope: durable relational schema, coordinator-only roster/contact management, plots, configurable seasons/timezone, prior-season holdings, unique allocations and application timestamps, restricted seed/import workflow with validation and change history. Excludes: allocation UI and arbitrary gardener-editable household membership.
Acceptance: exactly 40 configured plots, valid March-October season dates, stable household identity, previous holders established; unique household-season and plot-season allocation enforced transactionally; contacts inaccessible outside coordinator-authorized server boundary. Behaviour: reject duplicates/invalid imports atomically with actionable errors; no sensitive logs. Verification: schema constraints and import/authorization tests. Prerequisites: P01. Assumptions: coordinator obtains accurate roster and historical records; auth plumbing arrives P05 before user-facing access.

P05 Passwordless access and roles (foundation), deps P01,P04.
Outcome: gardener signs in to own household and coordinator accesses privileged operations, source owner sign-in answer and brief.md Constraints.
Scope: emailed one-time links; signed sessions, single-use short expiry, rate limits, safe redirects, logout; coordinator provisioning; authorization across records and API; administrative roster binding. Excludes: passwords, self-service household merging, social login.
Acceptance: intended email recipient gets own records only; coordinator alone sees contacts/other households; expired/used link denied with resend; unrecognized emails receive non-enumerating response with plain path to coordinator enrollment; no account/role elevation from submitted IDs. Behaviour: link email failure recoverable, secret-safe logs and accessible auth feedback. Verification: token replay/expiry, session and cross-household authorization integration tests with sandbox email. Prerequisites: P01,P04. Assumptions: one sign-in email per household as approved.

P06 Seasonal application (allocation), deps P03,P04,P05.
Outcome: household applies for coming season selecting 0-3 preferences, source brief.md must 1.
Scope: authenticated mobile form, valid unique plot choices, eligibility from prior holdings, durable submit and receipt with pending status. Excludes: guaranteed preferences and self-service application editing.
Acceptance: one application per household-season, server timestamp and stable order, duplicate retries do not duplicate or move order, coming season shown clearly. Behaviour: invalid/closed season and stale data explained; retries safe; loading/success announced; no contact leak. Verification: form and API tests for 0/1/3/4 preferences, duplicates, retries, prior holder and cutoff boundaries. Prerequisites: P03,P04,P05. Assumptions: application eligibility window configured by coordinator; service validates open window.

P07 Allocation and ordered waiting list (allocation), deps P03,P06.
Outcome: coordinator allocates plots and puts remaining applicants into FIFO waiting list, source brief.md must 2/Rules.
Scope: application review with preferences; rule-enforced early returning-priority queue; transactional assign/reassign/release; batch transition of unallocated applications to waitlist; confirm FIFO promotion when plot released; preserve history.
Excludes: automatic preference optimization, notifications of allocations, offers/expiry.
Acceptance: no double plot/household allocation even concurrent requests; qualifying returning applicants processed before new applicants; priority does not reorder waitlist; stable original application order preserved through retries/transitions; promotion cannot skip queue; unavailable preferences do not silently discard applicant. Behaviour: stale/conflicting assignment rejected and refreshed, empty/full states explicit, destructive reassignment confirmed. Verification: core rule TDD, cutoff/timezone/tie fixtures, concurrent allocation and waitlist promotion integration tests. Prerequisites: P03,P06. Assumptions: within category FIFO; no preference guarantee; coordinator resolves exceptional withdrawal explicitly with audit so next promotion remains FIFO.

P08 Gardener allocation and coordinator map (allocation), deps P03,P07.
Outcome: gardener sees own plot/season and coordinator sees all 40 holders, source brief.md must 3/5.
Scope: own allocation view, awaiting/waitlisted status, season dates; coordinator-only grid and accessible equivalent list with holder names/empty plots. Excludes: public map or other-household details for gardeners.
Acceptance: 40 plots exactly, holders match canonical allocations, changes reflected after save/refresh, gardener own dates/plot correct. Behaviour: empty/loading/stale/error states, keyboard list navigation and large text; no sensitive browser cache after logout. Verification: end-to-end seeded full/empty allocation views, role isolation and phone/zoom checks. Prerequisites: P03,P07. Assumptions: grid is schematic, physical garden layout not supplied.

P09 Checkpoint: application and allocation demonstration (allocation), deps P08.
Criteria: owner sees mobile application, priority allocation, FIFO waitlist promotion, own allocation/season and private 40-plot map including conflict recovery. Artifact: working seeded demo. Verify recorded acceptance. Gates release acceptance only, not unrelated problem work.

P10 Gardener problem reports (problems), deps P03,P05,P07.
Outcome: gardener reports a problem on their allocated plot, source brief.md must 4.
Scope: plain-text report, durable plot/season/household linkage, created timestamp, idempotent submission and receipt/status.
Excludes: attachments, chat, email to gardener.
Acceptance: own allocated plot only, nonempty bounded text, duplicate submit safe, coordinator can retrieve durable report; no report without allocation. Behaviour: empty/error/retry states, accessible feedback, safe escaping. Verification: validation, authorization and retry tests plus mobile journey. Prerequisites: P03,P05,P07. Assumptions: textual reports sufficient.

P11 Coordinator problem resolution (problems), deps P10.
Outcome: coordinator lists open problems and marks resolved, source brief.md must 4.
Scope: accessible open list, plot/report details, resolve action and timestamp, status history. Excludes: messaging/escalations.
Acceptance: all open reports visible only to coordinator, resolved action idempotent and removes from open list without destroying history. Behaviour: empty/loading/conflict/error recovery, safe report rendering. Verification: role and state-transition tests, open-to-resolved end-to-end. Prerequisites: P10. Assumptions: no reopen action in first version.

P12 Daily new-report email (problems), deps P01,P10.
Outcome: coordinator receives one daily email listing new problem reports, source owner notification answer.
Scope: durable schedule in configured timezone; report selection since last successful digest, daily batch/outbox, private minimal summary, authenticated detail links; provider idempotency and delivery observability, retry/recovery and coordinator address configuration.
Excludes: immediate alerts, gardener notifications, empty daily email.
Acceptance: reports grouped once per scheduled day, resolution doesn't suppress new reports, failure doesn't advance successful watermark or lose reports; restart/retry uses stable batch/provider key; no other recipients/contact data. Behaviour: catch-up after missed run, empty queue quiet, ambiguous delivery handled using provider status/idempotency rather than blindly recreating send; admin can inspect failed status. Verification: fake clock with timezone/DST, downtime, concurrent scheduler, provider success/failure/timeout/retry and sandbox rendered email tests. Prerequisites: P01,P10. Assumptions: daily time/address/timezone configured before release; provider support assessed P01.

P13 Checkpoint: problem handling and daily email (problems), deps P11,P12.
Criteria: owner reviews phone report, open/resolved coordinator list and actual sandbox digest, including failure recovery. Artifact: working problem demo and sample email. Verify decision recorded; gates release acceptance.

P14 Deployment, recovery and privacy readiness (release), deps P08,P11,P12.
Outcome: coordinator can operate reliable private service, source brief.md Constraints and implied persistent journeys.
Scope: approved hosting/env, access control audit, data backup/restore rehearsal, secret management, email delivery monitoring, failed digest retry instructions, household correction instructions, retention proposal for owner, runbook; configure real season/timezone/digest schedule.
Excludes: unapproved purchases and sending live email without deployment authorization.
Acceptance: smoke journey on staging, backup restored and invariant checks pass, email failure recoverable, no contacts exposed to gardeners or logs; owner can follow concise runbook. Behaviour: failures observable without sensitive data; restore reconciliation prevents repeated digest sends where provider supports. Verification: staging access audit and restore/delivery failure drill. Prerequisites: P08,P11,P12. Assumptions: owner supplies deployment access/config before going live; retention decided at acceptance, no invented legal requirements.

P15 First-version regression and accessibility (release), deps P08,P11,P12.
Outcome: evidence demonstrates the complete brief on phones, source all first-version requirements/constraints plus owner answers.
Scope: integrated end-to-end scenarios across role boundaries, priority/date/FIFO/concurrency, auth, digest; keyboard/screen reader/zoom review and plain-language correction.
Excludes: invented performance targets or formal user research.
Acceptance: reproducible pass evidence for every source requirement, no known blocking correctness/privacy/accessibility defects; representative 40-plot/60-household fictional dataset. Behaviour: test failure produces reproducible finding and tracked fix, loading/empty/error states covered. Verification: automated suite and documented manual assistive/mobile walkthrough. Prerequisites: P08,P11,P12. Assumptions: support current phone browsers, record checked environments.

P16 Checkpoint: first-version acceptance (release), deps P09,P13,P14,P15.
Criteria: owner accepts every brief requirement and sign-in/digest answers, household assumptions, garden timezone/exact dates/digest time and operating/retention choices; reviews demo, verification evidence and runbook. Artifact: deployable release candidate. No automatic production launch. Ordinary ticket limitation disclosed.

P17 Launch approved first version (release), deps P16.
Outcome: households and coordinator can use accepted Plotbook, source first-version outcome.
Scope: owner-authorized deployment, configured real roster/history/40 plots, verify actual email delivery with approved recipients, production smoke checks and recovery instructions. Excludes: purchase or release before explicit launch authorization.
Acceptance: all critical journeys usable, no seed/demo data or publicly exposed contacts, rollback available, coordinator handoff recorded. Behaviour: launch failure rolls back or closes access without data loss; no undocumented credentials. Verification: authorized production smoke and coordinator signoff. Prerequisites: P16 and owner launch approval. Assumptions: hosting/domain/email credentials available.

Coverage: must 1 P06; must 2 P07; must 3/5 P08; must 4 P10-P11; household uniqueness/returner cutoff/FIFO P04/P06/P07; phone/plain language/large text P02/P03/P15 and all UI slices; contact privacy P04/P05/P08/P14/P15; emailed one-time link P05; daily email P12; seasons/40 plots/prior holdings P04; deferred payments and tool lending explicitly no v1 tickets. Ownership checkpoints P03/P09/P13/P16.
Setup package: after explicit approval create .story with p0 plus four milestones and 17 todo tickets and above dependencies; AGENTS.md (purpose/boundary/planned architecture/TBD stack and configuration), RULES.md (domain/privacy/auth/retry rules and TDD), REVIEW.md verbatim supplied template; git init and ignores .story/snapshots/, .story/sessions/, .story/status.json. No GitHub issues imported.
Quality level Full pipeline because allocation state/business rules, privacy and durable notification workflow. No commands established: WRITE_TESTS and TEST proposed TBD test command selected P01; BUILD TBD build command selected P01; VERIFY TBD server start/readiness selected P01. All four explicitly disabled until concrete commands and tests exist, enabling in P01 after evidence and approved scope. No npm default fabricated for generic project. Snapshot, setup note and initial handover carry coverage/review/assumptions/pending tooling. This is planning only: no setup writes before package approval.
STORYBLOQ_PLAN"

The proposed setup gives **Plotbook 17 tickets across four milestones**, plus Storybloq’s initial Setup phase. It covers all five first-version requirements, emailed sign-in links, and the coordinator’s daily problem-report email. Payments and tool lending remain deferred.

Phases represent demonstrable milestones; tickets are specific work items. After setup, `$story` loads this context for future sessions.

**Proposed assumptions**

- The coordinator maintains household records, with one sign-in email per household.
- Initial allocation opens on **1 February**, preserving priority for returning gardeners who apply before the cutoff.
- Preferences are optional, distinct, and not guaranteed. Waiting-list order cannot be bypassed through direct assignment or reassignment.
- Daily emails include newly reported problems, even if subsequently resolved; no email is sent when there are none.
- Garden timezone, exact season dates, and daily email time must be configured before launch.
- Framework and provider selection belongs to the foundation ticket; no technology is represented as already established.
